source.howDecided: git log 3cf2963cd0..origin/main returns zero commits for packages/lib/server-only/recipient/create-envelope-recipients.ts, and the blob is byte-identical between v2.16.0 and v2.17.0 (58d5e68bd1 at both), so line numbers have not drifted. Read the region at origin/main: the only per-recipient assertion is still the loop at lines 87-92, `for (const recipient of recipientsToCreate) { assertCompatibleRecipientRole({ signatureLevel: envelope.signatureLevel, role: recipient.role }); }`, which keys on signatureLevel alone. Nothing between lines 62 and 97 reads envelope.documentMeta.signingOrder, and no PARALLEL or SEQUENTIAL comparison appears anywhere in the file. The bound docs are also byte-identical to the tested revision: apps/docs/content/docs/concepts/recipient-roles.mdx and apps/docs/content/docs/users/documents/add-recipients.mdx both hash the same at v2.16.0 and v2.17.0, so the restriction is still published verbatim at the same line numbers the review cited.

Unchanged: closed unmerged 2026-06-22 (merged=false), base main, head fix/assistant-always-first, 6 files +82/-38. Never landed, so the docs still forbid the combination while the API still allows it.
Unchanged. Origin of the role and of the UI-only enforcement.

reevaluation: The finding stands, unchanged in every respect. The culprit file is byte-identical between the tested tag and v2.17.0, the two doc pages that state the restriction are byte-identical too, and both cited upstream items are in exactly the state the review recorded (#2973 open and untouched since 2026-06-13, #2995 closed unmerged). Nothing among the 135 issues and PRs opened between 2026-08-01 and 2026-08-19 touches the assistant role or signing order, and a direct 'assistant' search over the whole tracker surfaces no report of the API accepting the combination. The review's fixedAfter claim ('live on main as of 2026-08-15') is still true one release later. No change to verdict, confidence or scope.
policyBasis: CONTRIBUTING.md: 'The most useful contribution is a detailed issue. Treat it like a spec. The more detail, the better: the problem you're trying to solve, and who it affects; how you expect the feature or change to behave; edge cases, constraints...'. Nothing in SECURITY.md applies; this is an unenforced product rule, not a vulnerability.
notes: Frame the issue as 'no refusal at all, the recipient is created', not as 'wrong status code': no doc page publishes a status for this refusal, and the scenario's expected 400 was the test's inference. Cross-link #2973 in the body and say plainly that there are two acceptable resolutions, enforce the documented rule server-side or change the docs and the workflow the way #2973 asks, because a maintainer reading this cold will otherwise think the two conflict. Two extra facts worth including because they raise the stakes beyond a contract violation: with signingOrder PARALLEL, send-document.ts notifies everyone at once so signers can act before the assistant, and getRecipientsForAssistant and getFieldsForToken filter on `signingOrder: { gte: assistant.signingOrder ?? 0 }`, which is NULL-false in SQL for the null signingOrder an API-created parallel recipient carries, so the assistant's own view comes back empty. Also state that a complete fix must cover update-envelope-recipients and the envelope-meta path, since flipping an envelope back to PARALLEL while an ASSISTANT exists reaches the same illegal state from the other side.
